goals: Mechanistic: quantify sensitivity of ELM sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) to soil texture across the basin
Validation: constrain simulated slow states against sparse USGS well water-table data (weak, analog-level only)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM with per-column SSURGO soil directly isolates texture control on native drainage; low relief + CONUS NLDAS means forcing is near-uniform, so soil is the clean varying factor.

answerable: Sensitivity of natural gravity sub-surface drainage/recharge (QDRAI) to soil texture, with forcing held near-uniform so texture is isolated
Rank of texture classes by drainage magnitude and by soil-moisture retention

not_answerable.aspect: Tile-drain discharge control by texture (the literal 'drainage' of an agricultural landscape)
not_answerable.why: ELM has no tile-drainage/managed-drainage representation; QDRAI is natural gravity drainage only, and no tile-drain flow observations exist in-domain
not_answerable.needs: tile-drainage process representation in ELM + tile-drain flow observations

not_answerable.why: observations_missing lists tile-drain flow; no in-domain flux dataset to compare against

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 5 dominant SSURGO texture classes spanning the drainage-relevant gradient (high-K sand to low-K clay), x3 replicates each to separate texture signal from within-class variation in soil depth/organic content; elevation is NOT a stratifier because 160 m relief yields negligible forcing variation and is not part of the question.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns on cultivated/agricultural land units and on the mapped dominant texture polygons; oversample lowland/valley soils where drainage and shallow water table interact most strongly, while ensuring each texture class is represented on typical (not edge) map units.
sampling_strategy.replication: 3 replicates per texture class to estimate within-class spread and confirm the texture signal exceeds intra-class noise.

sampling_plan.reason: high-conductivity end-member: expected maximum QDRAI, sets upper bound of texture sensitivity.
intermediate texture; samples the mid-range of the drainage response curve.
dominant agricultural soil in the basin; anchors the response at the most areally representative texture.
low-conductivity, moisture-retentive class where drainage suppression begins.
low-conductivity end-member: expected minimum QDRAI, sets lower bound of texture sensitivity.

validation_design.comparison: aggregated / analog — sparse wells cannot be co-located with every texture column; compare distribution of simulated warm-started WTD against well observations as a plausibility check, not a per-column calibration
none — declared GAP; no in-domain flux data and no tile-drain process in model

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing (near-uniform across basin), per-column SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.capability: WTD-informed warm start (Fan 2013) or multi-year spin-up
requires_capabilities.why: drainage/recharge and water table are slow states; cold start pins all columns at default WTD and reads QDRAI~0 during storage fill
requires_capabilities.blocks: any meaningful QDRAI comparison across texture classes

requires_capabilities.why: agricultural drainage is dominated by artificial tile networks the model does not represent
requires_capabilities.blocks: answering the question about actual agricultural drainage flux vs natural gravity drainage

requires_capabilities.why: no in-domain flux dataset to validate drainage against
requires_capabilities.blocks: direct validation of the QDRAI target

requires_capabilities.why: the entire stratification depends on resolving dominant texture classes and assigning per-column soil

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well WTD ingest + HUC boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: needed to locate sparse wells and clip domain for the analog water-table check

assumptions: NLDAS-2 forcing is effectively uniform over this low-relief basin, so texture is the isolated varying driver.
SSURGO resolves at least the five texture classes assumed; actual dominant classes will be set by the raster sampler.
QDRAI is interpreted as natural gravity sub-surface drainage/recharge, explicitly NOT tile-drain discharge.
Warm-started slow states carry some drift from Fan's lateral equilibrium; this drift is treated as an expected result, not calibrated away.
open_questions: Are the sparse USGS wells screened in the shallow aquifer relevant to ELM's ZWT, and how many fall inside the HUC?
Is the scientific interest in natural recharge (answerable now) or in tile-drain flow (needs new process + data)?
Should replication instead be spent widening texture classes if SSURGO reveals more than five dominant textures?
